newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOUTH AFRICA BATTLING RED LOCUST INVASION.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH AFRICA BATTLING RED LOCUST INVASION.

text.p: South Africa's agriculture department warned on Thursday that it was fighting swarms of red locusts which could invade the country's major crop producing areas.
The current locust invasion was the first into South Africa since the 1940s.
The department said in a statement that swarms of locusts had invaded the country's Northern Province while some had progressed as far as the Pretoria district.

"It is imperative that swarms be prevented from invading the major crop production areas of South Africa as this is a living pest and a voracious feeder on a wide range of crops and other plants," the statement said.
It said the migratory locusts bred in the Buzi flood plains in Mozambique.
"International control efforts appear to have been ineffective in containing the pest," the department said.

Neighbouring Zimbabwe said on Wednesday some of the country's food crop from the new November/April season may be destroyed by remnants of red locust swarms which invaded the country in August but later moved into Botswana.
The locusts, which moved in from neighbouring Mozambique last month, destroyed around Z$2 million worth of crops in the Matabeleland region which was hardest-hit by the swarms.
